description:
A runtime type test for pid, ref or c_pointer is always true. RuntimeTypePredicate (src/runtime_type_predicate.rs) has no axis for these opaque types, so the planner emits a test node that admits every value.

Probe (interp and run): def f(p :: pid), do: :matched, called with a received 1.5, prints :matched. Expected: FunctionClauseError, as def f(x :: integer) gives for a float.

Consequence for externs: after fz-xxd.15 an extern's typed parameters are tested at entry, but a pid, ref or c_pointer parameter still admits anything. In lib/ that is fz_send(pid, t) reached from the untyped Kernel.send (send(1.5, msg) is an unchecked raw-word read), and libc fclose, fgetc, ferror, fflush, fwrite and fz_file_read_line taking c_pointer. No lib extern takes a ref parameter.

One concept: each opaque runtime kind has a predicate axis, so its type test reads the value's kind like every other test. First confirm how pid, ref and c_pointer values are represented at run time on the three paths.

Fails before, passes after: fixtures on interp, run and build where a pid-, ref- and c_pointer-typed clause refuses an integer, float, atom, binary and list and admits the genuine value; send(1.5, :m) raises instead of reading a raw word.

Acceptance: full gate green; no pin rises unexplained.
title: A pid, ref or c_pointer type test tells those values from every other value
